slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students produce /h/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /h/, students repeat three times, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for hesitation or imprecise production of /h/.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students produce /e/ quickly and cleanly.

slides.teacher_cue: Before we begin: say the sound r — curl your tongue back without touching. This is the hardest sound for Korean learners. Mirror work begins today and continues every lesson.
slides.expected_response: Students attempt /r/ production with tongue curl before formal introduction.
slides.correction_move: Model with mirror — tongue curls back, no contact. Students copy.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution or Korean flap /ɾ/ — note any students who struggle before instruction begins.

slides.teacher_cue: Quick review — sight word. Say it as a whole unit. Use it in a sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students say I immediately without blending.
slides.correction_move: Model I in a sentence, point to the underline, repeat chorally.
slides.observation_note: Watch for hesitation or blending attempts — sight word should be instant recognition.

slides.expected_response: Students say the immediately without blending.

slides.teacher_cue: Play hen once. Replay only if needed before checking.

slides.teacher_cue: Tongue tip curls back — it does not touch the roof of the mouth. Lips slightly rounded. Voice on. Hold a mirror — you should not see your tongue tip. This is the voiced post-alveolar approximant. Mirror sessions are mandatory from this lesson at every review.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /r/ with correct tongue curl and no contact with the palate.
slides.correction_move: Show contrast in mirror: /l/ — tongue tip touches ridge, contact visible. /r/ — tongue curls back, no contact. Students alternate slowly before attempting words.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution, Korean flap /ɾ/, or tongue touching the palate. Note who needs extended mirror work.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect r to one strong word from today.
slides.expected_response: Students say r clearly and connect it to a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.

slides.teacher_cue: Say rat orally — a small rodent. Confirm /r/ production before revealing print. Blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rat orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model rat orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset. Redirect immediately with mirror.

slides.teacher_cue: Say ran orally — past tense of run. Confirm /r/ onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say ran orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model ran orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ onset and for dropping the final /n/.

slides.teacher_cue: Mime tearing paper and say rip. Confirm /r/ onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rip orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model rip orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ at onset and for the short /ɪ/ vowel quality.

slides.teacher_cue: Describe a rack as a frame for storage. Say the word, confirm /r/ onset. Reveal print and blend. ck is one unit — taught in the previous lesson.
slides.expected_response: Students say rack orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model rack orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ onset, accurate ck unit recognition, and final /k/.

slides.teacher_cue: A rick is a large stack of hay. Say rick orally, confirm /r/ onset. Reveal print and blend. ck is one unit.
slides.expected_response: Students say rick orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model rick orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ onset substitution and confirm ck is read as a single /k/ unit.

slides.teacher_cue: Rap means to knock sharply — rap on the door. Say the word, confirm /r/ onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rap orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model rap orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ onset substitution on rap. Contrast rat / rap — same onset, different coda.

slides.teacher_cue: Vocabulary warm-up. Say the word, connect meaning, then read it together.
slides.expected_response: Students read risk accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the word, then repeat chorally and point to each part if needed.
slides.observation_note: Watch for smooth oral reading before it appears in connected text.

slides.teacher_cue: Read it, track the parts, and confirm that every part fits the taught pool for r.
slides.expected_response: Students read the word accurately and explain why it is safe to read.
slides.correction_move: Tap each sound or chunk, blend, then reread smoothly.
slides.observation_note: Use this as confidence-building cumulative review, not as a surprise challenge.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build rat left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build rat correctly: r | a | t.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of rat, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students place every sound correctly, especially the target phoneme.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build rip left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build rip correctly: r | i | p.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of rip, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students place every sound correctly, especially the target phoneme.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build rick left to right. ck goes together in one slot.
slides.expected_response: Students build rick correctly: r | i | ck.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of rick, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset and confirm ck is placed as a single unit.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build rack left to right. ck goes together in one slot.
slides.expected_response: Students build rack correctly: r | a | ck.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of rack, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset and confirm ck is placed as a single unit.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build risk left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build risk correctly: r | i | s | k.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of risk, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students place every sound correctly, especially the target phoneme.

slides.teacher_cue: A is a sight word. rat and ran are decodable. Confirm /r/ production in both words before reading.
slides.expected_response: Students read "A rat ran." accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution in rat and ran during connected reading.

slides.teacher_cue: A and a are sight words. All other words decodable. Read the full sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students read "He ran at a rat." accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch for consistent /r/ production across the two /r/ words in one sentence.
